title: Distinct group-like elements in a coalgebra are linearly independent
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $C$ be a $k$-vector space with $k$-linear maps $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_k C$ and $\varepsilon:C\to k$ satisfying $(\Delta\otimes1)\Delta=(1\otimes\Delta)\Delta$ and $(\varepsilon\otimes1)\Delta=(1\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta=1_C$, where $C\otimes_kC$ and the tensor products of linear maps are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], under the canonical tensor associativity and unit identifications. Such data are a counital coassociative coalgebra. An element $g\in C$ is group-like if $\varepsilon(g)=1$ and $\Delta(g)=g\otimes g$. The set of group-like elements of $C$ is linearly independent over $k$: for every finite subset $S$ of distinct such elements, $\sum_{g\in S}a_g g=0$ with $a_g\in k$ implies $a_g=0$ for every $g\in S$.
